title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics to Spend $4.9B on AI Server Chip Substrates in Korea and Vietnam
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 28, 2026

Samsung Electro-Mechanics (KRX: 009150) will invest KRW 6.78 trillion (about US$4.9 billion) across South Korea and Vietnam to expand FC-BGA production for AI servers, its largest-ever investment in a single product line. Unusually, the company said global customers are partly funding the buildout and have guaranteed mid-to-long-term order volume. Here is what was approved, what a customer-backed capex deal like this means, and what still is not disclosed.

The board approved the Sejong investment on September 28. All four outside directors attended. Samsung Electro-Mechanics said the amount and schedule could still change as the projects proceed.

What FC-BGA is

FC-BGA (flip-chip ball grid array) is a high-density package substrate that sits between an advanced chip — an AI accelerator, GPU or CPU — and the main circuit board, carrying both power and high-speed data signals between them. As AI chips pack in more transistors and move more data, the FC-BGA under them needs more layers, larger surface area and finer wiring, which is why it has become a bottleneck component in AI server production.

The unusual part: customers are funding the buildout

According to the report, unnamed global big-tech and semiconductor customers are partly funding the new equipment and have committed to mid-to-long-term purchase volumes. That is a different, more concrete kind of evidence than the general "the industry expects more demand" framing common in this space: a capital-intensive line was greenlit with committed customer money and guaranteed orders attached, which lowers Samsung Electro-Mechanics' investment risk and helps secure a baseline utilization rate. CEO Jang Duk-hyun said in the announcement that "advanced semiconductor substrates are becoming a core component that determines both chip performance and supply-chain stability," and that the company will strengthen its FC-BGA competitiveness in AI, server and automotive markets.

What is still not named: the report does not identify which companies are providing funding or guaranteeing volume. We do not name a specific chipmaker as a confirmed customer, because none was disclosed.

Part of a bigger national push

The investment is described as part of the Korean government's "Korea Great Leap Forward" mega-project initiative. In July, at a public briefing on advanced industry in the Chungcheong region, Samsung previewed roughly KRW 8 trillion in combined spending on Sejong FC-BGA production capacity, core R&D and workforce development — a figure that appears to already include the KRW 4.27 trillion Sejong capex confirmed in this filing.

Quick FAQ

How much is Samsung Electro-Mechanics investing in AI chip substrates?
KRW 6.78 trillion total: KRW 4.27 trillion in Sejong, South Korea, and KRW 2.51 trillion in Vietnam.

Who is funding it?
Samsung Electro-Mechanics itself is the investor of record, but the company says unnamed global customers are contributing some of the capital and have guaranteed future order volumes.

What does FC-BGA do?
It is the substrate that connects a high-performance chip — such as an AI accelerator, GPU or CPU — to a server's main board, carrying power and data signals between them.

Is this the same as the "glass substrate" story?
No. Our September 28 market close brief covered a separate rally in glass-substrate stocks driven by market expectation, not a confirmed announcement. This FC-BGA investment is a distinct, disclosed capital commitment by one specific company.
